findings.name: Sensitive Administrative Directory and Multi-Framework Path Exposure
findings.description: The application exposes multiple platform-specific administrative paths such as /wp-admin/, /pv-admin/, and /admin-portal/. While some directories may return 403 or 404 depending on the current routing or WAF configuration, their exposure acts as a vector for credential stuffing, brute-forcing, and vulnerability scanning. WhatWeb and Wappalyzer also report mixed signatures (Joomla vs React/Tailwind), indicating potential reverse-proxy complexities or legacy systems running in parallel. Standard passive directory scans often miss these due to custom routing architectures or Web Application Firewall filtering, but custom active crawling reveals these routes.
findings.impact: An external attacker can map the administrative attack surface, identify the underlying CMS structure, and execute targeted administrative exploits or brute-force attacks against exposed login panels.
findings.remediation: Restrict access to all administrative directories (/pv-admin/, /admin-portal/, /wp-admin/) to trusted IP ranges using Nginx access controls or your WAF. Ensure that legacy directories that do not exist return a standard 404 page that does not disclose system details. Example Nginx config: location ~ ^/(pv-admin|admin-portal|wp-admin) { allow 192.168.1.0/24; deny all; }

findings.name: Insecure Cookie Attributes: Missing Secure Flag
findings.description: The application sets 'XSRF-TOKEN' and 'tops_technologies_session' cookies without the 'Secure' attribute. This allows the cookies to be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections if a user is tricked into making a non-HTTPS request, exposing sensitive session data to interception via man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks. Furthermore, the 'XSRF-TOKEN' cookie lacks the 'HttpOnly' flag, permitting client-side scripts to access it. Modern front-end architectures utilizing React often read tokens client-side, but this increases exposure to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) data theft.
findings.impact: Interception of session cookies or anti-CSRF tokens, leading to session hijacking or unauthorized action execution on behalf of authenticated users.
findings.remediation: Configure the application's session manager and cookie middleware to enforce the 'Secure' flag for all cookies. For PHP/Joomla/Laravel, ensure 'secure' is set to true in session/cookie configs. In Nginx, ensure headers are adjusted, or configure the backend directly. Example Laravel/PHP adjustment in config/session.php: 'secure' => true, 'http_only' => true.

findings.name: Obsolete and Insecure X-Frame-Options Header Configuration
findings.description: The response headers contain the 'x-frame-options: ALLOW-FROM www.learnvern.com' directive. The 'ALLOW-FROM' directive is obsolete and ignored by almost all modern web browsers (including Chrome, Safari, and modern Firefox). While the 'content-security-policy: frame-ancestors' header is present and acts as a modern fallback, reliance on obsolete headers can create security gaps on legacy user agents or trigger inconsistent parsing behaviors. Standard automated vulnerability scanners might ignore this due to the presence of CSP, but deep manual analysis highlights the vulnerability surface.
findings.impact: Potential Clickjacking attacks targeting legacy or non-compliant web clients, allowing external origins to render the site inside an iframe.
findings.remediation: Remove the obsolete 'X-Frame-Options: ALLOW-FROM' header and solely rely on Content-Security-Policy's 'frame-ancestors' directive, or set 'X-Frame-Options' to 'SAMEORIGIN' or 'DENY' if compatibility is needed, letting CSP handle granular origin controls. Example Nginx fix: add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always; add_header Content-Security-Policy "frame-ancestors 'self' www.learnvern.com;" always;
findings.evidence: x-frame-options: ALLOW-FROM www.learnvern.com, content-security-policy: frame-ancestors www.learnvern.com

findings.name: DNS Infrastructure Exposure and Name Server Misconfiguration
findings.description: The domain 'tops-int.com' uses nameservers located at 'VULNBOT.PRO'. Additionally, standard ANY and TXT DNS queries returned connection refused errors. This indicates potential DNS resolution inconsistencies, firewall restrictions blocking DNS diagnostic queries selectively, or use of a third-party managed DNS infrastructure that may lack redundant routing or expose structural vulnerabilities of the managing entity. This structure suggests a DNS-level security configuration that could be bypassed via direct IP communication if origin addresses are leaked.
findings.impact: An adversary can target the custom nameserver infrastructure (VULNBOT.PRO) or exploit DNS resolution discrepancies to execute Denial of Service (DoS) or cache poisoning attacks.
findings.remediation: Ensure nameservers are hosted on highly available, DDoS-protected, and enterprise-grade DNS networks. Correct any DNS resolver configurations causing 'ECONNREFUSED' on standard queries, and ensure DNSSEC is enabled and signed properly.
